todos: Create a WinUI 3 and .NET 10 migration branch plan that treats the existing WPF app as replaceable and keeps WiX Burn as the installer channel.
Update SDK, target framework, build props, and scripts for .NET 10 LTS and Windows 10 1809 build 17763 minimum support.
Add the Windows App SDK stable dependency and verify the current stable version before implementation.
Replace the WPF app shell with a WinUI 3 app shell using NavigationView pages for Presets, Search, Updates, and Activity.
Split the solution into Domain, Application, Infrastructure, and WinUI Presentation layers with one-way dependencies.
Redesign the package domain model around package identity, preset, selection, action, operation plan, operation status, and validation results.
Rebuild winget command execution behind infrastructure interfaces for command running, output parsing, package search, package resolution, update loading, and operation execution.
Create a new workspace storage schema and local state file without automatic migration from existing WPF-era data.
Implement new import and export support for the new onlywinget preset format only.
Rebuild preset management in WinUI with batch selection, add, edit, remove, rename, import, export, save, and apply flows.
Rebuild package search in WinUI with search execution, selectable results, package resolution, and add selected packages flow.
Rebuild updates in WinUI with refresh, selectable updates, apply selected updates, row status, error, and resolution output.
Implement reusable WinUI table, command bar, empty state, loading state, error state, and log/activity components.
Implement select-all behavior in reusable selection state logic so header clicks toggle all rows reliably from checked, unchecked, and mixed states.
Rebuild operation progress, cancellation, log buffering, and activity history so long winget operations remain observable and cancellable.
Preserve Italian and English localization in the new presentation layer and validate all visible command labels.
Update WiX Burn and MSI packaging to install or prerequisite the Windows App Runtime required by Windows App SDK.
Update installer OS checks, app payload harvesting, shortcuts, icons, and version metadata for the WinUI and .NET 10 output.
Port existing unit tests to the new Domain, Application, and Infrastructure layers and remove tests tied only to deleted WPF implementation details.
Add tests for storage schema, command builders, winget parsers, error classification, operation planning, selection state, and command availability.
Run format, lint, typecheck, test, build, package, and check scripts after the WinUI migration compiles.
Manually validate the WinUI app at minimum, default, and maximized window sizes in Italian and English.
Manually validate preset, search, update, activity, cancellation, and select-all flows on a Windows host with winget installed.
Run winget smoke tests with -RunWingetSmoke on a machine with winget installed and configured.
Run elevated package lifecycle validation on a clean or dedicated Windows host, including install, uninstall, upgrade, and winget source update.
Run the hosted GitHub Actions build-gate workflow for the exact release commit before tagging.
